start_here: Say to your AI: "Check every line of my film's SCRIPT.md against my made-up-base rules, using my made-up film readers setting." It reads your settings row and rules, reads each line of the script, and says pass, fail or uncertain for each with the rule it broke.

lists.holds: One node of your rule tree: a branch (a kind of thing you make) or a check (words, a pattern or a question that fails or holds a thing made), each naming the node it is part of.

values.says: No glitter in a spoken line.

key-value settings in a notes app

instructions: 1. Pour the example rows into your own lists (see pour for list:checks), or make list:checks and list:settings from them. Keep the settings row under the record id record:setting:check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts~person~made-up (the tool is allowed to read only record ids that start with record:setting:check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts~).
2. Read your film's copy files into text: for a script table, the name SCRIPT.md and its Markdown text.

3. Say "Check my film's script against made-up-base." The AI calls tools:run at @workshop-tools with tool tool:check-a-films-copy and { branch, settings_record, files: [{ name, text }] }. It reads only; nothing is written.

4. Read status and exit_code (0 passed, 1 failed, 2 unqualified, 3 uncertain), then results line by line (text, kind, where, verdict, breaks) and lines. Fix each failing line and run it again; send any questions it lists back in answers.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for your writing rules and its fields. The tool matches each kit field to one of yours (by the map you give, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), refuses when fewer than 80% match, and otherwise answers the records:write that adds the example rows to your list, leaving your own rows untouched.
